what: Layer 2 of Annex H: per frontend family, with what each rule is measured and with which default threshold. Whatever the annex declares is here; whatever the annex leaves to the project is published as UNDECLARED, never with an invented value. The tool names in the example of the annex (section 7) are illustrative and are therefore NOT copied here: a tool named in this data would read as a default, and it is not one.

layers.1: agnostic core: the statement of the rule, the same in every project, not negotiable
layers.2: adapter per frontend family: with what it is measured and with which starting threshold
layers.3: project decisions: the concrete thresholds and the exceptions, declared by the owner and never by the agent

annex_columns.note: The table says with what each of those six is measured in each family. The text of every cell lives only in the annex: what goes here is the pointer.

measured_by.in: a single configuration file per project
measured_by.note: The annex shows the SHAPE of the file, not final values. An installation that takes those names as defaults is inventing layer 2.

the condition of the CQ-18 escalation (D-048): declared true the rule blocks, declared false the escalation is DECLINED with a record, and undeclared is reported as an undeclared threshold, which means the escalation is PENDING and nobody looked at it. Those two are not the same state and before this id there was no key in which to tell them apart: the rule said the escalation is declared through the same mechanism as any threshold and no threshold id existed for it, so the absence of a declaration meant both things at once. The spelling of the id follows the words the rule already uses (outside the organisation), because ids are append-only and are never renamed. It is a boolean and not a number: what a threshold declares is a value, and the value here is whether the condition holds.

undeclared_threshold: it is reported as an undeclared threshold. No approximating, no silent inheriting and no inventing: the same rule as the sizing of the architecture step.
